result.title: Fast Muscle-Driven Whole-Body Motion Tracking with a Differentiable World Model
result.summary: Tracking motion capture with a whole-body musculoskeletal model means coordinating hundreds of muscles through contact, and current controllers take hours to days of GPU time to train, so every tuning decision is expensive. SuperMimic trains a tracking policy by backpropagating through the rollouts of a learned world model. We extend it to MS-Human-700 (700 muscles) and MyoFullBody (354 muscles), with MuJoCo's activation dynamics inside the world model. To make its training fast, our recipe takes the speedups developed for the Unitree G1, replaces three of their settings that fail on muscles, and adds four changes of our own: observations without muscle geometry, data collection concurrent with the updates, Beta exploration noise that keeps every excitation in $[0,1]$, and 50 Hz control. On one RTX 5090 it trains MS-Human-700 in 6.3 minutes to the held-out return that SuperMimic's published hyperparameters reach in 3.9 hours, 37$\times$ sooner, and in 20 minutes to lower tracking errors than theirs after 10 hours. It trains MyoFullBody 34$\times$ sooner without retuning. Ablations show what is specific to muscles: a higher policy learning rate stalls half of the runs, and clipped Gaussian noise adds a tonic co-contraction that Beta noise avoids. Finally, refining the policy's actions through the world model at test time lowers the position error by a further 26% with no held-out clip failing, and reaches the same return after 5.1 instead of 6.3 minutes of training. Code, the training recipe and videos are on the project page https://muscle-supermimic.beanpow.top.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 SuperMimic「在可微世界模型的 rollout 上反传梯度」的训练方式扩展到 700 与 354 肌肉的全身肌骨运动跟踪，通过更换观测、并行数据采集、Beta 探索噪声与 50Hz 控制等配方，把训练时间缩短 34–37 倍，并在测试时借世界模型细化动作，再降 26% 位置误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉或多模态推理无直接关系，但其「沿世界模型 latent rollout 传播梯度」和「推理期用世界模型迭代细化动作」可为 LVR 的 latent 轨迹训练、贡献分配与测试时状态细化提供可供核查的方法线索。
